answer: The best sybil defense is slow trust: an agent's influence equals account age times honest epochs, each epoch a settlement window whose promises, payments, and attestations all verified. New accounts start near zero weight, so minting a hollow identity is like sailing a voyage into a windless lagoon: an attacker spawns a fleet overnight, but each copy sits inert for months, paying compute and collateral before it can vote. Splitting one identity multiplies cost while influence grows sublinearly, so dominance costs more than honest history.
